scenes.heading: Watermarking
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Watermarking and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: Why watermarks exist
items: Bound how long state is kept
Let old windows finalize and drop
scenes.narration: Watermarking solves the problem of late data in event-time stream processing. It tells Spark how long to wait for stragglers before considering a time window complete. Crucially, it also bounds how much state Spark must keep, so old windows can be finalized and their state dropped instead of growing forever.

scenes.heading: How a watermark advances
steps: Data older than watermark is late
scenes.narration: Spark tracks the maximum event-time it has observed in the stream. The watermark is that maximum minus your configured lateness threshold, so it trails the newest data by a fixed amount. Any event whose time falls below the current watermark is considered too late and is dropped. Once the watermark passes a window's end, that window is finalized and its state is released.

scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import window, col

counts = (events
    .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes")
    .groupBy(window(col("event_time"), "5 minutes"), col("device"))
    .count())

(counts.writeStream.outputMode("append")
   .option("checkpointLocation", "/chk/w").format("parquet")
   .option("path", "/out/w").start())
scenes.heading: Windowed aggregation with a watermark
scenes.narration: Here withWatermark declares that event_time may lag by up to ten minutes, so Spark waits that long before closing each five-minute window. Data arriving more than ten minutes late relative to the watermark is discarded. The watermark makes append mode safe for this aggregation, because Spark now knows when a window is final and can emit it exactly once. Without it, Spark would have to keep every window's state indefinitely.

scenes.text: A longer watermark tolerates later data but holds more state.
scenes.narration: Choosing the lateness threshold balances correctness against resource use: a longer window catches more stragglers but keeps state around longer. Set it from your data's real observed lateness, not a guess.
